# Section 040: Audit Trails And Compliance Evidence

Makes the reader able to produce the evidence a platform must keep: who did what in the API (audit logs) and whether the cluster meets its policies (Kyverno policy reports and Gatekeeper audit results). It follows the policy section because the policy engines are the compliance sources.

**Curriculum item covered:** Generating Audit Trails and Enforcing Policy Compliance (SBOM, Compliance Reports, etc.)

---

## What You Will Master

- Write an audit policy that records Secret access at Metadata level, Deployment changes at RequestResponse and drops noisy read events
- Turn on audit logging by editing the kube-apiserver static pod manifest with the policy file, log path and volumes
- Confirm the API server restarted with the new flags and find the problem when it does not come back
- Find who deleted a Deployment, with which identity and when, in the audit log with jq
- Name the audit level and stage of a given event and say why a rule matched it
- Read a Kyverno PolicyReport and list which workloads fail which rule, with kubectl and with custom columns
- Read Gatekeeper audit results from a Constraint's status and name each violating object
- Pull the audit events for one compliance question (who changed a Deployment, who read a Secret) as evidence
- Choose which source answers a given auditor question (what breaks policy now, what changed, who did it)
- Explain why an Audit-mode policy and Gatekeeper audit report existing objects that admission never saw

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Record API Activity With Audit Logging
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Record API Activity With Audit Logging](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-01/playground` — kind cluster with no audit logging configured. Starfleet workloads in `starfleet`. A background `CronJob` named `deck-cleaner` in `outpost` running as service account `deck-cleaner` with rights to read Secrets and delete Deployments in `starfleet`, which every few minutes reads a Secret and deletes and recreates the `probe` Deployment (the activity to find in the log). The reader opens a shell on the control plane node container with docker exec or podman exec; `jq` is available on the node or the reader copies the log out.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-040/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Produce Compliance Reports From Policy Engines
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Produce Compliance Reports From Policy Engines](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-02/playground` — kind cluster with Kyverno 1.19.1 and Gatekeeper 3.23.1 installed. Two Kyverno ClusterPolicies in Audit mode (require resource limits, disallow the latest tag) and one Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate with a Constraint in dryrun enforcement (require an `owner` label on Deployments), all already producing results. Starfleet workloads in `starfleet`; `probe` has no limits and no `owner` label, and a `legacy-beacon` Deployment uses an image with the `latest` tag (the violations to find). API server audit logging already turned on by the bootstrap with a short Metadata-level policy, so audit events exist to read. No SBOM or vulnerability scanner.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-040/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Audit Trails And Compliance Evidence Capstone — `sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS021.git -c sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** An auditor asks three questions about the `starfleet` namespace: which identity deleted a Deployment in the last hour, which workloads fail the platform's Kyverno policies, and which objects violate the Gatekeeper `owner` label constraint. The reader turns on audit logging with a given policy, then writes each answer to a given file. The grader checks the audit log, the answer files and that the answers match the live reports.
